scienceAssessments.assessment: Caloric is explicitly a superseded historical explanation. Conserved energy is distinguished from heat as energy transferred because of temperature difference; heat is not described as a stored state quantity.

Friction and drilling illustrate mechanical energy becoming internal energy without requiring heat supplied from outside. Heating, ignition and bearing damage are conditional possibilities, not inevitable outcomes. Source examples remain descriptive rather than newly assigned experiments.

Internal heat balance is restricted to a system exchanging no energy with its surroundings and doing no work, with internal heat exchange as the process. The text does not elevate heat to a generally conserved substance. Heating by heat transfer and by work can produce the same temperature change under suitable experimental conditions, not for arbitrary unrelated Q and A or arbitrary processes.

The source-bound Joule mercury calorimeter, falling weights, rotating blades A and figure references 37/38 are retained. Only initial and final kinetic energies are identified as equal; kinetic energy is not claimed constant during motion. Control/correction of external heat exchange conditions qualifies the experimental comparison.

The footnote explicitly adopts positive work by the falling weight on the apparatus and uses the magnitude of its gravitational-potential-energy decrease. It does not confuse positive work with signed final-minus-initial potential energy, introduce an unsupported equation or generalize the ideal experiment to arbitrary energy-loss conditions.

The calorie is an energy unit, not an amount of material. Original 4.19 and 4.1868 joules per calorie are explicitly scoped to the source's unit convention rather than asserted as a universal value for all calorie definitions. Original water specific heat 4190 is retained as a lesson approximation, not an exact temperature-independent material constant. The legacy degree wording is identified as a temperature interval, not absolute temperature.

history.assessment: Each historical declaration occurs in both source and modern text with its own source-block reason. Original 1798 and the nineteenth-century Joule context remain. No fictional replacement, new historical date, unsupported priority claim or modernized measurement was introduced.
history.limitation: This is source-bound instructional-history review, not new archival verification of every historical apparatus description.

safety.assessment: The rubber-to-face instruction is not retained as student procedure. High-temperature machining and fire-making carry explicit hazard language, with no independent trial encouraged. The mercury/falling-weight apparatus is explicitly a historical description not to be independently constructed or repeated. No new procedural steps, exposure thresholds or medical claims are supplied.
